questions.question: Explain how to choose between a bar graph, a histogram and a line graph for a new dataset, giving the test applied to the horizontal axis.
questions.expected_answer: Ask what the horizontal axis carries. Named separate groups (flavours, provinces) take a bar graph with gaps — nothing exists between categories. Numerical intervals tiling a continuous number line (marks 0–9, 10–19) take a histogram with touching bars. A quantity measured repeatedly over time takes a line or broken-line graph with points joined in time order.

questions.question: Cola holds 45% of the drinks pie. Calculate its slice angle, and the number of colas if 240 drinks are sold in the same proportions, naming the 'whole' used in each calculation.
questions.expected_answer: Angle: the whole is the 360-degree circle, so 0,45 × 360 = 162 degrees. Amount: the whole is the 240 drinks, so 0,45 × 240 = 108 colas. Same fraction, two different wholes; shares must total 100% and angles 360 degrees as a check.

questions.question: Using the takings data (380, 420, 150, 460, 510), give the three-layer interpretation: facts, trend, and a supported reason for the exception.
questions.expected_answer: Facts: lowest R150 on Wednesday, highest R510 on Friday, range R360, total R1 920. Trend: rising across the week — Friday is R130 above Monday. Exception with reason: Wednesday breaks the trend; a plausible, data-supported reason is early closing for sports, removing the lunch-rush customers.
